papers.title_en: Hybrid Gaussians for Robust Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation with Multi-View Object Association and Boundary Refinement
papers.authors: Xueqi Qiu, Yueming Sun, Tianyu Zhang, Yuxuan Xia, Yang Long
papers.evidence: 带边界优化的开放词汇三维分割
papers.tldr: 开放词汇3D分割在真实图像序列中面临2D监督不完整/噪声导致多视图身份分配不稳，以及全场景语义学习削弱对象级判别力的问题。论文提出Hybrid Gaussians统一3D表示，联合建模对象关联与语言对齐语义，并引入多视图对象关联（观测融合+语义对比学习）和边界重建优化。在LERF上达到59.1% mIoU，较基线相对提升13.4%，在3D-OVS上也表现优异。为鲁棒开放词汇3D分割提供了有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Open-vocabulary 3D segmentation localizes objects from free-form text queries, but remains challenging in real image sequences: incomplete or noisy 2D supervision destabilizes multi-view identity assignment, while full-scene semantic learning weakens object-level discriminability. We introduce Hybrid Gaussians, a unified 3D representation jointly modeling object association and language-aligned semantics. Its Multi-View Object Association mechanism combines Observation Fusion and Semantic Contrastive Learning to improve identity consistency and semantic discrimination. Boundary Reconstruction Optimization further refines local boundary structure to improve contour quality. Experiments on LERF and 3D-OVS demonstrate strong quantitative and qualitative performance. Our method achieves 59.1\% mIoU on LERF, yielding a 13.4\% relative gain over the baseline. Project page: https://nora202.github.io/hybridgaussians.

papers.title_en: Privacy-Preserving Semantic Segmentation from High-Resolution Depth and Ultra-Low-Resolution RGB
papers.authors: Xuying Huang, Swithinraj Moses Daniel, Sicong Pan, Sebastian Houben, Maren Bennewitz
papers.evidence: 结合深度与低分辨率RGB的语义分割
papers.tldr: 移动机器人相机带来隐私风险，超低分辨率RGB可从源头降低视觉暴露，却严重削弱语义与空间理解。为此，论文提出高分辨率深度加超低分辨率RGB的非对称感知设置，并设计2D联合框架，用HR几何引导语义RGB重建与RGB-D分割，再扩展为2D-to-3D流水线聚合语义特征完成3D分割，从而在限制外观信息的同时保留密集几何信息。在ScanNet上，该法取得隐私保护方法中最佳2D/3D分割，并零样本迁移至SUN RGB-D和SceneNN；隐私可恢复性下降，真机实验验证3D语义可用于目标导航。
papers.abstract_en: As mobile robots become increasingly integrated into everyday environments, privacy risks arising from onboard cameras have become a growing concern. Ultra-low-resolution (ULR) RGB can mitigate visual privacy exposure at the source, but ULR appearance alone substantially limits semantic and spatial understanding. We therefore introduce a privacy-preserving asymmetric sensing setting that combines high-resolution (HR) depth with ULR RGB, preserving dense geometry while restricting fine-grained visual information. To address the severe information imbalance between HR depth and ULR RGB, we propose a joint 2D framework using HR geometry to guide semantic-oriented RGB reconstruction and RGB-D segmentation. Despite reliable frame-level predictions, consistent scene-level understanding remains challenging under the asymmetric HR depth--ULR RGB setting. We therefore develop an end-to-end 2D-to-3D pipeline that consolidates 2D semantic features for 3D segmentation. Experiments on ScanNet show that our method achieves the best 2D and 3D segmentation performance among privacy-preserving approaches and delivers the strongest zero-shot transfer to SUN RGB-D and SceneNN. Privacy recoverability analysis shows that our proposed HR depth--ULR RGB input reduces the recoverability of sensitive data, and real-robot experiments demonstrate the utility of the resulting 3D semantics for object-goal navigation.
